# 2 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Maccabees 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/2MA_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Preamble

Chapter 2 concludes the second letter (vv. 1–18) with the story of Jeremiah hiding the ark, and then provides the author's formal literary preface (vv. 19–32), explaining that this book is an epitome of Jason of Cyrene's five-volume history. The preface is a remarkable piece of Hellenistic literary self-consciousness. EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA agree on the substance but differ on register, particularly in the preface.

---

**1** One finds also in the records that Jeremiah the prophet ordered those who were being deported to take some of the fire, as has been mentioned,

**2** and that the prophet, after giving them the law, charged those who were being deported not to forget the commandments of the LORD, and not to be led astray in their thoughts when they saw the gold and silver idols and their ornamentation.

**3** And with many such exhortations he urged them that the law must never depart from their hearts.

**4** The same writing also records that, moved by a divine oracle, the prophet ordered that the tent of meeting and the ark should accompany him as he went out to the mountain where Moses had climbed and had seen the inheritance of God.

**5** When Jeremiah arrived, he found a cave there. He brought in the tent, the ark, and the altar of incense, and he sealed the entrance.

**6** Some of those who had followed tried to mark the path so they could find the way back, but they were unable to.

**7** When Jeremiah learned of this, he rebuked them and declared: "The place shall remain unknown until God gathers his people together again and shows his mercy.

**8** Then the LORD will disclose these things, and the glory of the LORD will appear, together with the cloud — as they appeared to Moses, and as Solomon asked when he prayed that the place might be greatly hallowed."

**9** It was also made clear that Solomon, possessing wisdom, offered a sacrifice at the dedication and completion of the temple.

**10** Just as Moses prayed to the LORD and fire came down from heaven and consumed the sacrifices, so also Solomon prayed and fire came down and consumed the whole burnt offerings.

**11** And Moses said, "Because the sin offering was not eaten, it was consumed in the fire."

**12** In the same way Solomon kept the eight days.

**13** These same things are also reported in the records and the memoirs of Nehemiah: how he founded a library and gathered together the writings about the kings and the prophets, the writings of David, and letters of kings concerning votive offerings.

**14** In the same way Judas also gathered together all the writings that had been scattered because of the war that had come upon us, and they are now in our possession.

**15** If you have need of them, send someone to obtain them.

**16** Since we are about to celebrate the purification, we write to you. You will do well to observe these days.

**17** It is God who has saved all his people and has given to all the inheritance and the kingdom and the priesthood and the consecration,

**18** as he promised through the law. We trust in God that he will soon have mercy on us and gather us from everywhere under heaven to the holy place, for he has rescued us from great evils and has purified the place.

**19** This is the account of Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, and of the purification of the great temple, and of the dedication of the altar,

**20** and further of the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,

**21** and of the appearances that came from heaven to those who strove zealously for Judaism, so that, though they were few, they plundered the whole land and drove off the barbarian hordes,

**22** recovered the temple renowned throughout the whole world, freed the city, and restored the laws that were about to be abolished — all because the LORD in his great clemency became gracious toward them.

**23** All these things, which were set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five volumes, we shall attempt to condense into a single book.

**24** Considering the flood of material and the difficulty facing those who wish to engage with this history because of the mass of numbers,

**25** we have aimed to please those who wish to read, to make it easy for those who wish to memorize, and to be of use to all who take up the book.

**26** For those of us who have taken on the labor of abbreviation, it is not an easy task but one requiring effort and late hours,

**27** just as it is no light thing for one who prepares a banquet and seeks to benefit others. Yet to win the gratitude of many we will gladly undertake this difficult work,

**28** leaving the precise treatment of every particular to the historian, and striving to follow the rules of a summary account.

**29** For as the architect of a new house must attend to the whole structure, while the one who undertakes the encaustic work is concerned only with what is fitting for decoration — so it is with us.

**30** To enter into the details and range over the whole subject belongs to the author of an original history;

**31** but the one who produces an epitome should be permitted to aim for brevity and to forego exhaustive treatment.

**32** Here, then, let us begin the narrative, saying no more by way of preface — for it is foolish to compose a long introduction and then abridge the history itself.

---

## Translator's Notes

- **vv. 4–8, the Ark narrative**: This passage is unique to 2 Maccabees and has no parallel in the Hebrew Bible. It presents Jeremiah hiding the ark on Mount Nebo (where Moses died), linking the two great prophets. The location is consistent with Deuteronomy 34 geography.
- **v. 13, Nehemiah's library**: This is an important early reference to the collection of Hebrew scriptures. The list — "writings about the kings and the prophets, and the writings of David, and letters of kings" — corresponds roughly to the Former Prophets, Latter Prophets, Psalms, and possibly Chronicles.
- **v. 23, Jason of Cyrene**: Nothing further is known of this historian. His five-volume work does not survive; 2 Maccabees is our only access to his material.
- **vv. 26–32, the epitomist's preface**: This is genuine Hellenistic literary theory. The comparison to a dinner party host, the architect vs. the muralist — these are standard rhetorical topoi of the period, demonstrating the author's Greek literary education.
